questions.text: Is climate action the core purpose or goal of the policy?
questions.answer: The policy, titled 'Climate Ready Whittlesea', is primarily focused on climate action. The core purpose of the policy is to ensure that the City of Whittlesea is taking necessary actions to adapt to ongoing changes in climate. The policy is intended as an organisational document, focusing on ensuring that services and assets are taking into consideration the latest science to build a vibrant and resilient city. The policy also outlines the role of local government in climate change adaptation, which includes developing and delivering locally-appropriate adaptation responses, building the resilience of local assets and services, and planning for emergency management at the municipal level. The policy also aims to help the community understand and get involved in climate change adaptation.

This plan has been developed to ensure that the City of Whittlesea is undertaking the necessary actions to ensure that our organisation is adapting to the ongoing changes in our climate.

questions.text: Does the document show evidence of policy experimentation in climate action? Here we define experiments as initiatives to test technologies, policies and governance approaches on a small scale and under real world conditions. They are often referred to as pilots, initiatives, test beds, demonstration projects, and urban laboratories.
questions.answer: The documents provide evidence of policy experimentation in climate action. The local government has implemented a project in partnership with Deakin University and the local farming community, known as the Land Capability Project. This project is an example of a real-world experiment, testing the potential of agriculture in the rural north of the municipality under two separate climate change scenarios. The project combines scientific modelling with local farmers' knowledge to provide robust localised data on the potential for agriculture in the municipality. This approach allows the local government to understand the implications of climate change on the local agricultural sector and plan for future changes. The project is still underway, indicating an ongoing commitment to experimentation and adaptation in response to climate change.
